extracted.intended_audience: researchers and engineers building or evaluating automated / AI-assisted peer review systems; ML/AI conference reviewers, conference organizers, and authors seeking pre-submission automated feedback
extracted.subtask_description: Generation and automatic evaluation of structured, conference-style peer reviews for ML/AI conference papers using a specialized LLM fine-tuned on expert reviews. Covers data collection, prompt design, model training, demo interface, evaluation metrics and ethical/deployment guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write reviews in markdown and follow the review template
rubrics_metrics.description: The system prompt specifies that the review must be written in markdown format and follow a specific review template, which is part of the input and differs across venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a review template as input; allow users to edit the template to change sections/aspects/rating scales; generated reviews should adhere to the template's sectioning and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehend technical content and evaluate core scientific dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: A good reviewer has to comprehend technical content, including mathematics and empirical results, and evaluate the work’s contributions, novelty, significance, and methodological soundness according to high, field-specific standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should assess technical correctness, clarity of derivations/experiments, novelty relative to related work, significance/impact of results, and soundness of methodology; include concrete examples and evidence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow conference-specific reviewer guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReviewer is trained to follow standard review templates and guidelines, ensuring structured feedback that aligns with conference reviewing practices; system prompt is inspired by the ICLR 2024 reviewer guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align generated review structure, sections and rating scales with the target venue’s reviewer guide; allow template customization for different venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation Exact Match (EM) to human reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the generated review’s numerical recommendation exactly matches one of the human reviewers’ recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute EM across the test set; use as a metric for how often automated recommendations coincide with at least one human reviewer when normalized to the chosen scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average absolute recommendation error
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the average absolute difference between the generated review’s recommendation and the human reviewers’ average recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize recommendations to a common scale (here 1–10) before computing absolute error; report mean error and standard deviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalize recommendation scores to a 1–10 scale
rubrics_metrics.description: For cross-venue comparison, normalize recommendation scores to a scale from 1 (strong reject) to 10 (strong accept).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistent normalization when comparing recommendations across venues or models; report mean and dispersion after normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match human recommendation distribution / criticalness level
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated reviews should reproduce the distribution of human reviewer recommendations rather than tending to be overly positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare average recommendation and variance to the human reviewer distribution; avoid systematic positive bias (an anti-pattern noted for general-purpose LLMs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference evaluation with LLM-as-judge (Review Arena)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given expert reviews and two candidate reviews A and B, ask an LLM judge (GPT-4o in this work) to determine which generated review aligns better with the expert reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge should consider section-wise alignment with expert reviews and output A, B or Tie; report win rates of each model across the test set to compare quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge by section-wise matching to expert reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The LLM judge assesses how well each section of a generated review matches the corresponding section in the expert reviews before deciding which review aligns better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating judge prompts, explicitly instruct the judge to compare corresponding sections (e.g., strengths, weaknesses, methodology critique) and weigh overall alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use greedy decoding (temperature 0) for deterministic generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated reviews in evaluation were produced with greedy decoding (temperature 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use deterministic decoding to make comparative evaluation fair and reproducible across models; note that choice of decoding strategy affects style and variance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data: select earliest submission revision, avoid later camera-ready versions
rubrics_metrics.description: For each paper we obtain the earliest revision possible since later (camera-ready) revisions may already incorporate feedback from reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer originals/non-camera-ready versions to avoid leakage of review content into the paper; if double-blind originals are unavailable, acknowledge and manage non-anonymized data risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data preprocessing: accurate PDF-to-markdown extraction including equations and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert PDFs to markdown using a pipeline (Marker) that extracts text, applies OCR when needed, detects page layouts, preserves reading order, and converts equations/tables accurately — essential for scientific papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow users to inspect/edit converted markdown to fix conversion errors; prioritize tools that retain math and table fidelity since evaluation depends on technical content understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data filtering by length and reviewer confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter papers and reviews by length (remove top and bottom 1% quantile) and keep only high-confidence reviews using a reviewer confidence threshold roughly equal to “Confident, but not absolutely certain.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filtering reduces noise and outlier effects; document thresholds and report retained dataset size after filtering (79K reviews here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discard appendix content from training data
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix content is discarded and only the full text of the main and reference sections is retained for model training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide explicitly whether appendices are considered part of the reviewed content; if discarded, note potential information loss (e.g., detailed proofs in appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt design: system prompt conditions reviewer role and reviewer guidelines; minimal user prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReviewer uses a system prompt that conditions the LLM on its reviewer role and defines fixed reviewer guidelines; the user prompt is minimalistic ('Review the following paper:' followed by full paper text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed reviewer instructions (tone, structure, required sections) in the system prompt; keep user prompt simple to avoid leaking instructions inconsistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation methodological caution: similarity-to-human assumption limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation approach compares generated reviews to human reviews, which assumes that similarity to human reviews equals quality — an assumption with limits because human review quality/control is limited and experts disagree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement automated similarity measures with other metrics or human evaluation where feasible; explicitly acknowledge the assumption and its limitations in results discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report standard evaluation statistics (EM, avg error, mean recommendation ± std)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Exact Match (%), average recommendation error, average recommendation and standard deviations for each model to characterize alignment and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include confidence intervals or standard deviations to communicate variability; present baseline comparisons in tables for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use previous review-quality metrics (soundness, helpfulness, RQI) as complementary measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior work proposes metrics like soundness of reviews, helpfulness ratings, and structured quality instruments (van Rooyen et al.'s RQI) for assessing review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider incorporating these established instruments when evaluating generated reviews, especially with human raters, to measure dimensions beyond recommendation alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid data leakage and document anonymization issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial use of non-anonymized papers may introduce information leakage concerns into training and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document anonymization status of training data; consider masking author/institution cues or restricting use if risk of leakage could bias model outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical deployment rules: do not replace human peer review and include clear disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReviewer is not intended to replace human peer review; include explicit statements of limitations, promote responsible use, make code/model open, and encourage bias detection and mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear documentation of limitations, recommended use cases (pre-submission feedback), and safeguards to prevent misuse (e.g., not used as official reviewers); support community development of deployment guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interface affordances: let users edit converted text and the review template
rubrics_metrics.description: Demo shows the markdown conversion output which users can edit to fix conversion errors, and exposes an editable review template in an accordion element so users can deviate from defaults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose conversion outputs and templates to users to correct extraction issues and tailor the review format; streaming generation can improve perceived responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model design tradeoffs: specialized training vs model scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized training on peer review data helps overcome positive bias in general-purpose LLMs; a modest 8B parameter model balanced performance with accessibility and compute tradeoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing model size, consider the benefit of domain-specific fine-tuning; document tradeoffs and justify choices for accessibility and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report win rates in pairwise comparisons against baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: In the arena evaluation, report win rates of OpenReviewer vs other LLMs (e.g., 60%–76% wins against various baselines) as an interpretable comparative metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute win rates over a held-out test set using a consistent judge procedure; accompany with qualitative examples of wins/losses to interpret differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge domain and evaluation limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations include dataset restricted to 2022+ ICLR and NeurIPS, possible non-anonymized data, dependence on PDF conversion accuracy, small test set (400 papers), automated-only evaluation without human-in-the-loop, limited baseline set, and hardware constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list and discuss limitations; avoid overgeneralizing results beyond the domains and evaluation setup used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training procedure documentation and hyperparameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Document full training details (e.g., full-finetune Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for three epochs, effective batch size 64, learning rate 2×10^-5, max sequence length 128k, bfloat16 precision, Deepspeed ZeRO-3, Flash Attention V2, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide axolotl/deepspeed configs and all hyperparameters to enable reproducibility; report compute used (64 A100 80GB GPUs, ~34 hours) and any memory/throughput optimizations.
